papers.title: Influence of the Aging Time in the Hot Swaged Ti-12Mo-13Nb Alloy: Microstructure and Properties
papers.abstract: β-Ti alloys have been increasingly explored for biomedical applications due to their attractive combination of mechanical properties, including low elastic modulus, high tensile strength, good fatigue resistance, excellent ductility, and superior corrosion resistance. In this context, and building upon previous research, a metastable β-Ti alloy, Ti-12Mo-13Nb, was developed via hot forging as a potential alternative to the conventional Ti-6Al-4V alloy. This study investigates the microstructure and mechanical behavior of the Ti-12Mo-13Nb alloy processed by hot swaging, followed by aging at 500 °C for 10 min, 4 h, and 24 h. Phase transformations were analyzed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Mechanical characterization was carried out through Vickers microhardness testing and Young’s modulus measurements. The highest microhardness-to-modulus ratio was achieved after aging at 500 °C for 24 h, corresponding to a microstructure composed of fine α precipitates uniformly distributed within the β matrix.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索热锻Ti-12Mo-13Nb合金作为Ti-6Al-4V替代品的潜力。
summary_zh.method: 通过热锻和不同时效时间处理，利用XRD和TEM分析相变，测试显微硬度和弹性模量。

summary_zh.validation: 通过XRD、TEM及力学测试验证微观结构和性能变化。

summary_en.motivation: Investigate the potential of hot-forged Ti-12Mo-13Nb alloy as a substitute for conventional Ti-6Al-4V in biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Ti-12Mo-13Nb was processed by hot swaging followed by aging at 500°C for different times; phase transformations were analyzed via XRD and TEM, and mechanical properties were evaluated by microhardness and Young's modulus measurements.
summary_en.result: Aging for 24 h yielded the highest microhardness-to-modulus ratio due to a microstructure of fine α precipitates uniformly distributed in the β matrix.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural and mechanical characterizations (XRD, TEM, microhardness, modulus) validated the property changes with aging time.

papers.title: The effect of Co additions on the microstructure and mechanical properties of solute lean ⍺ + β Ti alloys
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V is an α + β Ti alloy of great commercial significance to the aerospace sector, due to a good balance of mechanical properties. However, alloys that can be processed at lower temperatures whilst retaining these favourable mechanical properties could offer attractive financial and environmental benefits. As such, there has been recent interest in developing solute lean α + β Ti alloys which have been reported to improve on the room temperature ductility of Ti-6Al-4V. Despite this, there is currently a limited understanding of the role that specific alloying additions, namely Co, have on achieving these favourable properties. As such, this study considered the microstructure and mechanical properties of a systematic series of Ti-Al-V-Co alloys. Co was seen to influence the size of the different α populations in a bimodal microstructure and result in a shallower β approach curve. Furthermore, greater Co contents were seen to result in higher work hardening rates in the material. However, the precipitation of intermetallic phases identifies a limit to the fractions of Co that can be introduced before the ductility of such alloys becomes compromised.

summary_en.motivation: To understand the role of Co additions in solute lean α+β Ti alloys for improved ductility while maintaining strength.
summary_en.method: A systematic series of Ti-Al-V-Co alloys were fabricated and characterized using microscopy and tensile testing.
summary_en.result: Co influences α colony size and increases work hardening rate, but excessive Co leads to intermetallic precipitation degrading ductility.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical testing and microstructural analysis.
